components.name: Button - Primary

components.name: Stage Chip

narrative.overview:
Basmet Dawah's learner site is the arc of one day, dawn to evening, and every screen shows where the learner stands in it. The page is white and calm, warmed by soft tinted panels that carry the three learning stages as times of day: dawn coral for just beginning, daylight green for building the basics, evening indigo for growing deeper. This is a deliberate replacement of an earlier ink-on-white primer world: that system read as flat and joyless, so the build now favors color, comfortable illustration, and gentle lift over rule-and-ink austerity, while staying modern and minimal rather than ornamental. It also refuses the emerald-and-gold arabesque cliche common to Islamic-content sites.

One deep blue pill (--primary, #2b3990) carries the single next action on every screen: 'Find your starting point,' 'Continue,' 'Talk to a mentor.' Soft painterly illustrations of places and objects, dawn rooms, prayer rugs, lantern-lit corners, hillside paths, appear on every major surface; by explicit production rule they contain no people, no faces, no hands, and no text, letters, or calligraphy. Cards carry hairline borders and soft resting or lifted shadows rather than the flat, shadowless primer grid the previous system prescribed. Readex Pro sets every UI label and paragraph in English, Arabic, and Spanish; Amiri is reserved for set Arabic phrases quoted at readable scale.
keyCharacteristics: White page and surface, with soft dawn/day/evening tinted panels and gradient glows, not a flat ink-on-paper duotone
One deep blue pill button (--primary) per screen for the single next action; gold (--accent) reserved for small highlights, never buttons
Three stage colors (dawn coral, daylight green, evening indigo) carried on illustrations, stage marks, stage chips, and progress fills, never as a text kicker sitting above a heading
Soft resting shadow (--shadow-soft) and a stronger lift shadow (--shadow-lift) on cards, hero art, and hover states; this is not a flat, shadowless system
Soft painterly illustrations of places and objects only, no people, no faces, no hands, no text or calligraphy, on every major surface

rules.name: The One Pill Rule
rules.body: Every screen carries exactly one primary (deep-blue, filled) button for its single obvious next action. Every other action on that screen is secondary, quiet, or danger; a screen never shows two filled primary pills at once.

rules.name: The Stage-on-Substance Rule
rules.body: Stage color identity lives on illustrations, stage marks, stage chips overlaid on artwork, progress fills, and step-tab numerals. It is never rendered as a standalone label or kicker floating above a heading with no other function.

rules.name: The Gold-Is-Rare Rule
rules.body: Warm gold marks a small highlight and never becomes a button, a card fill, or a nav state; blue alone carries interactive weight.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Readex Pro sets every UI control and every paragraph in English, Arabic, and Spanish. A second typeface is never introduced for flavor; Amiri is a script-accuracy tool for quoted Arabic, not a display font.

rules.name: The Ambient Lift Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft and diffuse, doubled (a tight near shadow plus a broad far one) to read as gentle elevation, not as a hard, offset, cartoon-style shadow; that device belongs to a neobrutalist world this one is not.

dos: Do give every screen exactly one filled primary (deep-blue) pill for its one obvious next action (The One Pill Rule); every other action is secondary, quiet, or danger.
Do carry stage identity on illustrations, marks, chips overlaid on imagery, and progress fills, never as a bare kicker line above a heading (The Stage-on-Substance Rule).
Do keep every illustration people-free, face-free, hand-free, and text-free, matching the production rule in docs/illustrations.md; a new illustration prompt must restate that rule.
Do use small line icons (lucide, 16 to 24px, strokeWidth 1.75 to 2.5) for functional affordances; the build uses them natively throughout, inline and never in an icon font.
Do put answer, selection, and progress markers so they hold their visual position under RTL by using logical (start/end, inset-inline-*) properties, not fixed left/right.
Do treat Amiri-set Arabic phrases as self-contained islands: their own direction and unicode-bidi: isolate regardless of the surrounding page's language.
donts: Don't use warm gold for a button, a card fill, or a nav state; it is a small-highlight color only (The Gold-Is-Rare Rule).
Don't show a stage color as body text without its tint background or a contrast-checked on-stage/on-stage3 pairing on top of the solid fill.
Don't introduce a second display typeface for personality; Readex Pro carries every language and every role except quoted Arabic phrases.

Don't add a hard, offset, single-direction cartoon shadow anywhere; this world's depth is soft and ambient (The Ambient Lift Rule), and a hard-offset shadow belongs to a neobrutalist system this one is not.

Don't apply this system to the admin panel. Admin keeps its own incumbent slate/primary (blue/gold) styling; it is out of scope for this DESIGN.md and gains only new fields and lesson-block editors, not the learner-site visual language.
